extracted.intended_audience: inventors and patent applicants (clients of patent attorneys) preparing or reviewing a patent specification
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and checking a patent specification so it satisfies legal, technical and procedural requirements (structure, disclosure, claims, drawings, sequences, enablement). Intended to help applicants review a specification prepared by counsel before filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title
rubrics_metrics.description: A title to identify the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The title may be relatively uninformative if secrecy is desired because the application (including title and applicant) may be publicly visible soon after filing and the full specification usually publishes after 18 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement as to the field to which the invention relates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a brief paragraph summarising the field, framed as broadly as possible to help readers appreciate the greatest extent of the invention as described and claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background (state of the art / prior art)
rubrics_metrics.description: An explanation of the background 'state of the art' – what was already known prior to the invention, and relevant prior art documents known to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section sets the backdrop against which the invention is contrasted, highlighting non‑obvious technical contributions. Statements of objective technical problems arising in the art before the invention are of assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of the objective of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of an objective technical problem which the invention seeks to solve, or an objective the invention is aimed at achieving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State objectives that the invention seeks to overcome, but avoid making the stated objective too ambitious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements of invention (summary corresponding to claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements of invention which correspond in scope and content to the claims, including any statements of technical advantages achieved by the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include main statements corresponding to each independent claim (reciting essential features) and subsidiary statements corresponding to dependent claims (preferred or optional features). May include statements of advantage and possible variations/modifications. Sometimes a simple reference to the claims is used instead of separate statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of any drawings and brief summary of what they show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely identifies drawings; ensure the list correctly describes what each drawing shows so readers and examiners can follow the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description / specific examples (non‑limiting)
rubrics_metrics.description: A description of specific examples of the invention, often with reference to any drawings; by convention non‑limiting as to the scope of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full technical details so a person skilled in the art is enabled to work the invention across substantially the entire claimed range. Include as many embodiments and practicable variations as possible. Give precise ranges and examples (e.g., showing a working temperature range and best values, and indicating values outside the range that fail) to support breadth and enablement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — format (numbered single‑sentence paragraphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims are a series of numbered paragraphs, each containing a single sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must be drafted as numbered, single‑sentence paragraphs. Independent and dependent claims form a nested structure; dependent claims usually refer back to earlier claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — balance between novelty and breadth for independent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent claims must define something that is new and inventive compared with the prior art, yet also define the scope of protection as broadly as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent claims serve two conflicting purposes: be specific enough to distinguish over prior art (possibly requiring added detail during examination) while being as broad as possible to maximise protection. Strike a balance so every feature in an independent claim is essential to the working of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — dependent (subsidiary) claims as fallback and commercial coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependent claims recite preferred or optional features and form narrower, nested claims that provide fallback positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dependent claims to anticipate possible prior art, provide fallback positions if independent claims are unpatentable, and to cover expected commercial embodiments. Ensure subsidiary claims cover valuable technical alternatives not captured in the independent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — clarity, conciseness, and support
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims must be clear and concise and supported technically by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must be supported so that the extent of the claimed invention is credible from the description and exemplification. Ensure the invention as defined in the claims is enabled across substantially the entire range of claimed features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: An abstract summarising in general terms what the specification is about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract assists in official classification and helps third parties locate the application when searching; it may be brief and general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings (informal vs formal) and technical correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings that accompany the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial 'informal' drawings may be crude but must clearly show required information to control initial filing costs. Replacement formal drawings may be required later. Applicants should check drawings are technically correct and contain necessary information and advise of corrections prior to filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing (biological inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence listing (in cases involving nucleotide and amino acid sequences) presented as a text document in a particular format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listings enable patent offices to extract and search sequence information. Check that sequences and descriptors are correct; clerical errors are common. Notify counsel immediately of any revisions or updates arising from further sequencing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement / sufficiency of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must be disclosed in such complete terms that a person of average skill in the art can work the invention in substantially all the claimed areas without undue burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine trial and error to a reasonable degree is permissible but the skilled person must not face undue burden due to missing technical information. Counsel can suggest whether a specification might be sufficient but final factual judgment rests with technical experts; inventors should carefully review technical completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best mode disclosure (where required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of the 'best mode' known to the inventor of performing the invention (required by law in some countries, notably the USA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that an example of the best currently known embodiment is included where required; failure to include best mode can lead to refusal or other adverse consequences in some jurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art disclosure / duty of candour (U.S. specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of any documents that a reasonable examiner would consider material in deciding whether to grant a patent (onerous duty of candour in the United States).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the US, failure to disclose material prior art may invalidate patent rights even if the document would not have changed the examination outcome. For other jurisdictions, while not the same legal duty, promptly addressing newly discovered prior art is in the applicant's interest to safeguard rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client review checklist — claims, objectives, sequences, drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific items applicants should check in a specification prepared by counsel before filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clients should: verify prior art has been considered; confirm objectives and achievements are accurately stated; ensure the best mode is disclosed; check enablement and that the claims only recite essential features (think what a third party could omit to avoid infringement); flag technical features that could limit claims but still have commercial value and are not covered by dependent claims; ensure sequence listings are correct; and advise on better drawings if available.
